# cycle_dns_zone (Resource)

Manages a Cycle DNS zone. A zone represents a domain (origin) whose DNS records are either fully hosted by Cycle (`hosted = true`) or managed externally with only LINKED records handled by Cycle (`hosted = false`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A zone fully hosted by Cycle — Cycle serves all record types.
resource "cycle_dns_zone" "hosted" {
  origin = "example.com"
  hosted = true
}

# A linked zone — DNS stays with your existing provider and
# Cycle only manages LINKED records.
resource "cycle_dns_zone" "linked" {
  origin = "linked.example.com"
  hosted = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosted` (Boolean) Whether this zone is hosted by Cycle. When `true`, Cycle acts as the authoritative nameserver for the origin and serves all record types. When `false`, the zone is linked: DNS stays with your existing provider and Cycle only manages LINKED records.
- `origin` (String) The origin (domain name) of the DNS zone, e.g. `example.com`. Changing this forces a new zone to be created — zones cannot be renamed.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique ID of the DNS zone.
- `state` (String) The current state of the DNS zone (e.g. `new`, `pending`, `verifying`, `live`, `disabled`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# DNS zones are imported by zone ID.
terraform import cycle_dns_zone.hosted 651586fca6078e98982dbd90
```
